claim: Metabolic reprogramming toward aerobic glycolysis unavoidably induces methylglyoxal (MG) formation in cancer cells.
source: Metabolic reprogramming toward aerobic glycolysis unavoidably induces methylglyoxal (MG) formation in cancer cells.
evidence: This is a statement in the abstract that is supported by the established knowledge of glycolysis and MG formation, and is further supported by experimental data shown in the manuscript.

claim: MG mediates the glycation of proteins to form advanced glycation end products (AGEs).
source: MG mediates the glycation of proteins to form advanced glycation end products (AGEs).
evidence: This statement is supported by established scientific knowledge about MG biochemistry and is referenced in the introduction.

claim: MG-induced AGEs are a common feature of breast cancer.
source: We have recently demonstrated that MG-induced AGEs are a common feature of breast cancer.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous work by the authors (Chiavarina et al., 2014).

claim: Breast tumors with MG stress presented with high nuclear YAP.
source: Breast tumors with MG stress presented with high nuclear YAP, a key transcriptional co-activator regulating tumor growth and invasion.
evidence: This claim is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 1B and quantified in Figure 1C.

claim: Elevated MG levels resulted in sustained YAP nuclear localization/activity that could be reverted using Carnosine, a scavenger for MG.
source: Elevated MG levels resulted in sustained YAP nuclear localization/activity that could be reverted using Carnosine, a scavenger for MG.
evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 2D and quantified in Figure 2E.

claim: MG treatment affected Hsp90 chaperone activity and decreased its binding to LATS1, a key kinase of the Hippo pathway.
source: MG treatment affected Hsp90 chaperone activity and decreased its binding to LATS1, a key kinase of the Hippo pathway.
evidence: This claim is supported by Hsp90 ATPase activity assay data (Figure 7E) and co-immunoprecipitation data (Figure 7F).

claim: Cancer cells with high MG stress showed enhanced growth and metastatic potential in vivo.
source: Cancer cells with high MG stress showed enhanced growth and metastatic potential in vivo.
evidence: This claim is supported by mouse xenograft data shown in Figures 8 and 9.

claim: There is a positive correlation between carbonyl stress intensity and nuclear YAP detection in breast cancer (Rspearman = 0.3975, p=0.0001).
source: We demonstrated a positive correlation (Rspearman = 0.3975, p=0.0001) between carbonyl stress intensity and nuclear YAP detection.
evidence: This claim is supported by statistical analysis of immunohistochemistry data from 87 breast tumors shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Cytoplasmic YAP staining showed no significant difference between high and low/intermediate carbonyl stress breast tumors.
source: Cytoplasmic YAP staining showed no significant difference between high and low/intermediate carbonyl stress breast tumors (Figure 1D).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantification of immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: YAP was mainly localized in the nucleus of low-density cultured cancer cells.
source: YAP was mainly localized in the nucleus of low-density cultured cancer cells as detected by immunofluorescence.
evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A and D.

claim: When breast cancer cells reached confluence, YAP was not detectable in the nucleus and became generally less visible suggesting that it underwent degradation.
source: When breast cancer cells reached confluence, YAP was not detectable in the nucleus and became generally less visible suggesting that it underwent degradation (Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A and D).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 2A and supplementary figures, with the degradation aspect being an inference from the observation.

claim: Upon MG treatment, MDA-MB-231 cells showed a concentration dependent persistence of YAP in both the cytoplasm and the nucleus despite the cells reached confluence.
source: Upon MG treatment, MDA-MB-231 cells showed a concentration dependent persistence of YAP in both the cytoplasm and the nucleus despite the cells reached confluence (Figure 2A).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 2A and quantified in Figure 2B.

claim: Nuclear YAP immunodetection was dose dependently higher in MG treated cells when compared to untreated cells in high-density cultures.
source: Quantification supported that nuclear YAP immunodetection was dose dependently higher in MG treated cells when compared to untreated cells in high-density cultures (Figure 2B).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantification of immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: TAZ was modulated in the same way as YAP in breast cancer cells under MG treatment.
source: We next showed that TAZ, the YAP paralog in mammalian cells, was modulated in the same way in breast cancer cells under MG treatment (Figure 2—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3.

claim: Analysis of total YAP and TAZ expression using Western blot demonstrated their increase in MG-treated cancer cells.
source: Analysis of total YAP and TAZ expression using Western blot further demonstrated their increase in MG-treated cancer cells (Figure 2C and Figure 2—figure supplement 1C and F).
evidence: This claim is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 2C and supplementary figures.

claim: A decreased or a stable cytoplasmic P-YAP (S127 and S381) level was observed and was consistent with nuclear YAP accumulation upon MG treatment.
source: A decreased or a stable cytoplasmic P-YAP (S127 and S381) level was observed and was consistent with nuclear YAP accumulation upon MG treatment (Figure 2C and Figure 2—figure supplement 1C and F).
evidence: This claim is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 2C and supplementary figures.

claim: YAP mRNA levels were not significantly changed upon MG treatment in the three breast cancer cell lines.
source: YAP mRNA levels were not significantly changed upon MG treatment in the three breast cancer cell lines (Figure 2—figure supplement 1G).
evidence: This claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1G.

claim: When MDA-MB-231 cells were concomitantly treated with MG and carnosine, YAP cellular accumulation in high-density cultures was significantly returned to untreated cells basal level.
source: When MDA-MB-231 cells were concomitantly treated with MG and carnosine, YAP cellular accumulation in high-density cultures was significantly returned to untreated cells basal level (Figure 2D and E)
evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 2D and quantified in Figure 2E.

claim: Carnosine alone did not affect significantly cellular YAP immunodetection.
source: Carnosine alone did not affect significantly cellular YAP immunodetection.
evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 2D and E.

claim: GLO1 inhibition was achieved by the use of siRNAs and the use of S-p-bromobenzylglutathione cyclopentyl diester (BBGC), an effective Glo1 inhibitor.
source: First, GLO1 inhibition was achieved by the use of siRNAs on one hand and the use of S-p-bromobenzylglutathione cyclopentyl diester (BBGC), an effective Glo1 inhibitor on the other hand [Tikellis et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Tikellis et al., 2014 and experimental validation shown in Figure 3A and Figure 3—figure supplement 1C and D.

claim: MBo, a specific fluorescent sensor for MG in live cells, demonstrated endogenous MG increase upon Glo1 expression inhibition and BBGC treatment in MDA-MB-231 cells.
source: MBo, a specific fluorescent sensor for MG in live cells [Wang et al., 2013), demonstrated endogenous MG increase upon Glo1 expression inhibition and BBGC treatment in MDA-MB-231 cells (Figure 3A).
evidence: This claim is supported by fluorescence microscopy data shown in Figure 3A and citation to Wang et al., 2013.

claim: Both GLO1-depleted and BBGC-treated MDA-MB-231 cells displayed nuclear YAP persistence in high-density cultures.
source: Consistent with exogenous MG treatment experiments, both GLO1-depleted and BBGC-treated MDA-MB-231 cells (Figure 3A and B) displayed nuclear YAP persistence in high-density cultures.
evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 3A and quantified in Figure 3B.

claim: Similar results were obtained under both GLO1 silencing and BBGC treatment conditions in MDA-MB-468 cells.
source: Similar results were obtained under both conditions in MDA-MB-468 cells (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A and B).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A and B.

claim: MDA-MB-231 cells significantly increased their glycolytic activity when cultured in high glucose compared to low glucose.
source: Lactate measurement using 1H-NMR showed that MDA-MB-231 cells significantly increased their glycolytic activity when cultured in high glucose compared to low glucose (Figure 3C).
evidence: This claim is supported by 1H-NMR lactate measurement data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: In MDA-MB-231 cells, high-glucose culture induced elevated endogenous MG level that was assessed using both FACS detection of MBo fluorescent probe and LC-MS/MS quantification.
source: In these cells, high-glucose culture induced elevated endogenous MG level that was assessed using both FACS detection of MBo fluorescent probe (Figure 3D) and LC-MS/MS quantification (Figure 3E).
evidence: This claim is supported by FACS and LC-MS/MS data shown in Figure 3D and E.

claim: Similar results were observed in the other highly glycolytic breast cancer cell line, MDA-MB-468.
source: Similar results were observed in the other highly glycolytic breast cancer cell line, MDA-MB-468 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1E–G).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1E–G.

claim: Low glycolytic MCF7 cells did not react to high-glucose culture condition and kept stable lactate.
source: As expected, low glycolytic MCF7 cells used for comparison did not react to high-glucose culture condition and kept stable lactate (Figure 3C).
evidence: This claim is supported by 1H-NMR lactate measurement data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: MCF7 cells showed stable MG levels thus pointing for the first time to MG increase as a specific response of glycolytic cancer cells to glucose stimulus.
source: More importantly, MCF7 cells showed stable MG levels (Figure 3D and E) thus pointing for the first time to MG increase as a specific response of glycolytic cancer cells to glucose stimulus.
evidence: This claim is supported by FACS and LC-MS/MS data shown in Figure 3D and E, with the interpretation being an inference from the data.

claim: MDA-MB-231 and MDA-MB-468 cells cultured to confluence in high glucose demonstrated positive nuclear YAP and TAZ staining when compared with cells cultured in low glucose.
source: MDA-MB-231 and MDA-MB-468 cells cultured to confluence in high glucose demonstrated positive nuclear YAP and TAZ staining (Figure 3F and G and Figure 3—figure supplement 1H and I; and Figure 3—figure supplement 2) when compared with cells cultured in low glucose.
evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 3F, G and supplementary figures.

claim: YAP accumulation was not detectable in high-glucose MDA-MB-231 and MDA-MB-468 cells treated with 2-DG just like in low-glucose cultured cells.
source: As expected, YAP accumulation was not detectable in high-glucose MDA-MB-231 and MDA-MB-468 cells treated with 2-DG just like in low-glucose cultured cells (Figure 3—figure supplement 3C and D).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3C and D.

claim: MCF7 cells did not observe any significant persistence of YAP and TAZ.
source: As expected from their stable glycolytic rate and unaffected MG level (Figure 3C,D and E), we did not observe any significant persistence of YAP and TAZ in MCF7 breast cancer cells (Figure 3H and I and Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 3H, I and supplementary figures.

claim: MCF7 cells are able to induce YAP accumulation in response to an exogenous MG supply.
source: It is noteworthy that MCF7 cells are able to induce YAP accumulation in response to an exogenous MG supply (Figure 2—figure supplement 1)
evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: The observed effects of endogenous high MG levels on YAP were significantly reversed using 2 MG scavengers, carnosine and aminoguanidine in MDA-MB-231 cells.
source: Finally, the observed effects of endogenous high MG levels on YAP were significantly reversed using 2 MG scavengers, carnosine and aminoguanidine in MDA-MB-231 cells (Figure 3—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 4.

claim: Among the 14 YAP target genes tested, 8 genes including CTGF gene showed a significant increase at the mRNA level in GLO1 depleted cells when compared to control.
source: Among the 14 targets tested and known to be regulated positively by YAP, we found that 8 genes, including CTGF gene, showed a significant increase at the mRNA level in GLO1 depleted cells when compared to control (Figure 5A).
evidence: This claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Knock-down of YAP using siRNA transfection reversed, at least in part, the expression of all the evaluated genes.
source: Importantly, knock-down of YAP using siRNA transfection reversed, at least in part, the expression of all the evaluated genes thus establishing the link between YAP target genes expression and GLO1 status in cancer cells.
evidence: This claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: The expression of YAP target genes and GLO1 showed a significant inverse correlation in breast cancer patients.
source: Indeed, we found that the expression of YAP target genes and GLO1 showed a significant inverse correlation in breast cancer patients.
evidence: This claim is supported by correlation analysis using publicly available gene expression data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1B.

claim: In low-density cultured cells, YAP was bound to CTGF promoter, whereas in confluent cells, YAP was not detectable.
source: In low-density cultured cells, YAP was bound to CTGF promoter, whereas in confluent cells, YAP was not detectable which is consistent with YAP absence in the nucleus of high-density cells.
evidence: This claim is supported by chromatin immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: YAP was found at CTGF promoter in MG-treated confluent cells at a comparable level to that in sparse cells.
source: In contrast, YAP was found at CTGF promoter in MG-treated confluent cells at a comparable level to that in sparse cells (Figure 5B).
evidence: This claim is supported by chromatin immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: CTGF mRNA level was not significantly affected by MG treatment in MDA-MB-231 cells.
source: CTGF mRNA level was not significantly affected by MG treatment in MDA-MB-231 cells (Figure 5C).
evidence: This claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: MDA-MB-231 cells cultured in presence of MG and treated with TGF-β responded by a two-fold increase of CTGF mRNA level compared to TGF-β alone.
source: MDA-MB-231 cells cultured in presence of MG and treated with TGF-β (2.5 ng/ml) responded by a two-fold increase of CTGF mRNA level compared to TGF-β alone confirming the requirement of TGF-β pathway activation for MG-mediated induction of CTGF expression (Figure 5C).
evidence: This claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Smad2 and Smad3 phosphorylation following TGF-β treatment in MDA-MB-231 cells was not affected by MG treatment.
source: Smad2 and Smad3 phosphorylation following TGF-β treatment in MDA-MB-231 cells was not affected by MG treatment (Figure 5—figure supplement 2B)
evidence: This claim is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2B.

claim: YAP silencing prevented MG-mediated CTGF mRNA induction in presence of TGF-β in confluent MDA-MB-231 cells.
source: In agreement with this deduction, we showed that YAP silencing prevented MG-mediated CTGF mRNA induction in presence of TGF-β in confluent MDA-MB-231 cells (Figure 5D).
evidence: This claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: YAP and TEAD1 co-localized in MG-treated confluent MDA-MB-231 cells, and in sparse cultured cells used as positive control, whereas this co-localization was not detected in untreated confluent cells.
source: As shown in Figure 5E and Figure 5—figure supplement 2E, YAP and TEAD1 co-localized in MG-treated confluent MDA-MB-231 cells, and in sparse cultured cells used as positive control, whereas this co-localization was not detected in untreated confluent cells.
evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 5E and Figure 5—figure supplement 2E.

claim: At 72 hr, the increase in cell proliferation in GLO1-depleted cells was significantly abrogated upon YAP silencing.
source: At 72 hr, this increase in cell proliferation was significantly abrogated upon YAP silencing indicating that it is required to sustain MG-induced pro-growth effect (Figure 5F).
evidence: This claim is supported by DNA quantification assay data shown in Figure 5F.

claim: MG-treated MDA-MB-468 cells showed an increase of vimentin and a decrease of E-cadherin expression, attesting of an EMT process.
source: We observed an increase of vimentin and a decrease of E-cadherin expression, attesting of an EMT process in MDA-MB-468 cells treated with MG (Figure 5—figure supplement 3A).
evidence: This claim is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 3A.

claim: E-cadherin network was disrupted in MG-treated cells.
source: Next, we observed by immunofluorescence that E-cadherin network was disrupted in MG-treated cells (Figure 5—figure supplement 3B).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 3B.

claim: MG-treated MDA-MB-468 cells showed an enhanced migration potential that was efficiently reversed to basal level upon YAP silencing.
source: Consistent with EMT induction, MG-treated MDA-MB-468 cells showed an enhanced migration potential that was efficiently reversed to basal level upon YAP silencing (Figure 5—figure supplement 3C and D).
evidence: This claim is supported by wound healing assay data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 3C and D.

claim: LATS1 mRNA levels were not affected by MG in the three breast cancer cell lines.
source: LATS1 mRNA levels were not affected by MG in the three breast cancer cell lines (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The treatment of breast cancer cells with MG132 proteasome inhibitor induced LATS1 increase.
source: In good accordance, the treatment of breast cancer cells with MG132 proteasome inhibitor induced LATS1 increase (Figure 6B).
evidence: This claim is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: The use of MG132 proteasome inhibitor reverted MG-induced LATS1 decrease.
source: As shown in Figure 6B, the use of MG132 proteasome inhibitor reverted MG-induced LATS1 decrease.
evidence: This claim is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: When LATS1 was overexpressed, MG effects on YAP accumulation were reverted as assessed by immunofluorescence in MDA-MB-231 cells.
source: Accordingly, when we overexpressed LATS1, we were able to revert MG effects on YAP accumulation as assessed by immunofluorescence using two anti-YAP antibodies in MDA-MB-231 cells (Figure 6C and Figure 6—figure supplement 1B)
evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 6C and Figure 6—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The incubation of human recombinant Hsp90 with MG followed by MS analysis revealed the modification of several lysine and arginine residues notably yielding to the formation of carboxyethyllysine (CEL) and argpyrimidine/hydroimidazolone adducts, respectively.
source: The incubation of human recombinant Hsp90 with MG followed by MS analysis revealed the modification of several lysine and arginine residues notably yielding to the formation of carboxyethyllysine (CEL) and argpyrimidine/hydroimidazolone adducts, respectively (Figure 7—source data 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by mass spectrometry data referenced in Figure 7—source data 1.

claim: Immunoprecipitation of MG-treated MDA-MB-231 extracts using anti-argpyrimidine MG adducts and followed by Hsp90 immunoblot analysis allowed detection of a basal level of glycated Hsp90 in MDA-MB-231 glycolytic cells that was further enhanced upon MG treatment.
source: Immunoprecipitation of MG-treated MDA-MB-231 extracts using anti-argpyrimidine MG adducts and followed by Hsp90 immunoblot analysis allowed us to detect a basal level of glycated Hsp90 in MDA-MB-231 glycolytic cells that was further enhanced upon MG treatment (Figure 7A).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunoprecipitation and Western blot data shown in Figure 7A.

claim: Hsp27 was efficiently detected in argpyrimidine immunoprecipitates.
source: Hsp27, which is recognized as a major MG target in cancer cells, was also efficiently detected in argpyrimidine immunoprecipitates (Figure 7A).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunoprecipitation and Western blot data shown in Figure 7A.

claim: The reverse IP experiment using an anti-Hsp90 antibody allowed the detection of both argpyrimidine and hydroimidazolone MG-adducts of the expected molecular weight in MG treated cells.
source: Consistently, the reverse IP experiment using an anti-Hsp90 antibody allowed the detection of both argpyrimidine and hydroimidazolone MG-adducts of the expected molecular weight in MG treated cells (Figure 7B).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunoprecipitation and Western blot data shown in Figure 7B.

claim: Recombinant human Hsp90 (rhHsp90) was effectively modified by MG and was protected by carnosine MG-scavenger.
source: Recombinant human Hsp90 (rhHsp90) was effectively modified by MG and was protected by carnosine MG-scavenger as assessed using both anti-argpyrimidine and anti-hydroimidazolone antibodies in Western blot experiments (Figure 7D).
evidence: This claim is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 7D.

claim: MG decreased rhHsp90 activity to an extent that was comparable to that seen using 17-AAG.
source: Using an in vitro enzymatic assay, MG decreased rhHsp90 activity to an extent that was comparable to that seen using 17-AAG (Figure 7E).
evidence: This claim is supported by Hsp90 ATPase activity assay data shown in Figure 7E.

claim: Incubation of rhHsp90 with MG in presence of carnosine efficiently reversed the effect on Hsp90 activity.
source: Incubation of rhHsp90 with MG in presence of carnosine efficiently reversed this effect indicating for the first time that direct MG glycation of Hsp90 affects its ATPase activity (Figure 7E).
evidence: This claim is supported by Hsp90 ATPase activity assay data shown in Figure 7E.

claim: Both MG and 17-AAG decreased LATS1 expression in the three breast cancer cell lines under study.
source: Furthermore, both MG and 17-AAG decreased LATS1 expression in the three breast cancer cell lines under study (Figure 7—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This claim is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1C.

claim: LATS1 immunoprecipitates contained detectable Hsp90 however this interaction was disrupted in presence of MG in MDA-MB-231 cells.
source: LATS1 immunoprecipitates contained detectable Hsp90 however this interaction was disrupted in presence of MG in MDA-MB-231 cells (Figure 7F).
evidence: This claim is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 7F.

claim: Stably GLO1-depleted MDA-MB-231 cells that were grafted subcutaneously in mice showed an increased tumor weight and volume that reached significance for shGLO1#2-silenced clones.
source: Stably GLO1-depleted MDA-MB-231 cells that were grafted subcutaneously in mice showed an increased tumor weight and volume that reached significance for shGLO1#2-silenced clones (Figure 8A).
evidence: This claim is supported by mouse xenograft data shown in Figure 8A.

claim: Exploration of shGLO1 experimental tumors using immunoblotting revealed the effective in vivo induction of argpyrimidine adducts and a strong inverse relationship between GLO1 silencing and total YAP expression.
source: Further exploration of shGLO1 experimental tumors using immunoblotting revealed the effective in vivo induction of argpyrimidine adducts and a strong inverse relationship between GLO1 silencing and total YAP expression (Figure 8B and C).
evidence: This claim is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 8B and quantified in Figure 8C.

claim: In GLO1-silenced experimental tumors, there was a specific increase of YAP in the nucleus of tumor cells using immunohistochemistry.
source: In GLO1-silenced experimental tumors, we further demonstrated a specific increase of YAP in the nucleus of tumor cells using immunohistochemistry (Figure 8D and E).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 8D and quantified in Figure 8E.

claim: Elevated proportion of Ki67 positive cells in shGLO1 tumors sustained the observed increased tumor growth.
source: Elevated proportion of Ki67 positive cells in shGLO1 tumors sustained the observed increased tumor growth, as shown and scored in Figure 8D and E, respectively.
evidence: This claim is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 8D and quantified in Figure 8E.

claim: Grafted GLO1-depleted cells on the CAM showed increased growth as assessed by the measure of tumor volume and compared to control cells.
source: Grafted GLO1-depleted cells on the CAM showed increased growth as assessed by the measure of tumor volume and compared to control cells (Figure 8F and G).
evidence: This claim is supported by CAM assay data shown in Figure 8F and quantified in Figure 8G.

claim: YAP knockdown with two independent siRNAs demonstrated the causative role of YAP in MG-induced tumor growth.
source: Remarkably, YAP knockdown with two independent siRNAs further demonstrated the causative role of YAP in MG-induced tumor growth. Indeed, YAP silencing in shGLO1 cells efficiently reverted tumor growth to control levels (Figure 8F and G).
evidence: This claim is supported by CAM assay data shown in Figure 8F and G.

claim: Significant YAP nuclear localization was observed in CAM shGLO1 tumors.
source: As shown on mice experimental tumors, we observed significant YAP nuclear localization in CAM shGLO1 tumors (Figure 8H and I).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 8H and quantified in Figure 8I.

claim: Lung metastases were detectable already after 3 weeks in GLO1-depleted conditions but not in control condition.
source: The follow-up of the mice showed that lung metastases were detectable already after 3 weeks in GLO1-depleted conditions but not in control condition.
evidence: This claim is supported by observations from the mouse xenograft metastasis experiment.

claim: After 6 weeks post-tumor removal, metastasized tumors were observed in the lungs of GLO1-depleted mice (68%) when compared to control (20%).
source: After 6 weeks post-tumor removal, metastasized tumors were observed in the lungs of GLO1-depleted mice (68%) when compared to control (20%).
evidence: This claim is supported by observations from the mouse xenograft metastasis experiment.

claim: Human vimentin immunohistochemical detection revealed a significant increase of both number and size of metastatic foci in GLO1-depleted condition.
source: To evaluate further lung colonization, we performed human vimentin immunohistochemical detection that revealed a significant increase of both number and size of metastatic foci in GLO1-depleted condition (Figure 9A), as quantified in Figure 9B.
evidence: This claim is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 9A and quantified in Figure 9B.

claim: A significant decrease of lung colonization was observed in shGLO1 mice treated with carnosine when compared with control mice.
source: We observed a significant decrease of lung colonization in shGLO1 mice treated with carnosine when compared with control mice (Figure 9C and D).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 9C and quantified in Figure 9D.

claim: Cancer cell metabolism is characterized by an enhanced uptake and utilization of glucose through aerobic glycolysis.
source: Cancer cell metabolism is characterized by an enhanced uptake and utilization of glucose through aerobic glycolysis.
evidence: This is a statement of established scientific knowledge about cancer metabolism.

claim: This overactive metabolism switch leads unavoidably to the formation of potent glycating agents such as MG.
source: This overactive metabolism switch leads unavoidably to the formation of potent glycating agents such as MG.
evidence: This is a statement based on established biochemical knowledge about glycolysis and MG formation.

claim: MG-mediated carbonyl stress interferes with LATS1 kinase, without affecting LATS2 and Mst1/2 kinases, to induce sustained YAP and TAZ nuclear localization.
source: Here, we demonstrate that MG-mediated carbonyl stress interferes with LATS1 kinase, without affecting LATS2 and Mst1/2 kinases, to induce sustained YAP and TAZ nuclear localization.
evidence: This claim is supported by Western blot data showing selective LATS1 decrease (Figure 6B) and immunofluorescence data showing YAP/TAZ nuclear localization.

claim: The hypermethylation of the promoter region of LATS1 gene (50% of breast tumors) is associated with an aggressive breast cancer phenotype and poor survival.
source: The hypermethylation of the promoter region of LATS1 gene (50% of breast tumors) is associated with an aggressive breast cancer phenotype and poor survival (Takahashi et al., 2005).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Takahashi et al., 2005.

claim: LATS1 proteasomal degradation is favored in presence of MG.
source: We show in this study that LATS1 proteasomal degradation is favored in presence of MG
evidence: This claim is supported by Western blot data showing that proteasome inhibitor MG132 reverses MG-induced LATS1 decrease (Figure 6B).

claim: Three independent studies recently established a link between the Hippo-YAP pathway and cellular energy stress using a glucose deprivation strategy.
source: Three independent studies recently established a link between the Hippo-YAP pathway and cellular energy stress using a glucose deprivation strategy (DeRan et al., 2014; Mo et al., 2015; Wang et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to three studies.

claim: Under low-glucose condition an AMPK-LATS1 axis inhibits YAP activity.
source: These studies are in agreement that under low-glucose condition an AMPK-LATS1 axis inhibits YAP activity.
evidence: This claim is based on the cited studies (DeRan et al., 2014; Mo et al., 2015; Wang et al., 2015).

claim: Aerobic glycolysis impacts on YAP/TAZ transcriptional activity through a mechanism involving phosphofructokinase 1 binding to TEAD transcription factors.
source: Enzo and collaborators (Enzo et al., 2015) have recently demonstrated that aerobic glycolysis impacts on YAP/TAZ transcriptional activity through a mechanism involving phosphofructokinase 1 binding to TEAD transcription factors.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Enzo et al., 2015.

claim: A recent metabolic profiling study using breast cancer progression cellular models reported the induction of several glycolytic enzymes upon constitutive activation of YAP/TAZ factors.
source: A recent metabolic profiling study using breast cancer progression cellular models reported the induction of several glycolytic enzymes upon constitutive activation of YAP/TAZ factors (Mulvihill et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Mulvihill et al., 2014.

claim: Hsp90 is post-translationally glycated by MG for the first time.
source: We show for the first time that Hsp90 is post-translationally glycated by MG.
evidence: This claim is supported by mass spectrometry data (Figure 7—source data 1 and 2) and immunoprecipitation data (Figure 7A and B).

claim: Several post-translational modifications have been previously reported to affect Hsp90 stability and chaperone function.
source: Although several post-translational modifications have been previously reported to affect Hsp90 stability and chaperone function, our study importantly uncovers that a natural metabolite derived from glycolysis is involved in regulating Hsp90 in cancer cells.
evidence: This is a statement based on existing literature about Hsp90 modifications.

claim: Decreasing Hsp90 client binding has been considered as an attractive anti-cancer therapy because of its role in stabilizing the active form of a wide range of client oncoproteins.
source: Decreasing Hsp90 client binding has been considered as an attractive anti-cancer therapy because of its role in stabilizing the active form of a wide range of client oncoproteins and several synthetic Hsp90 inhibitors are now in clinical trials (Neckers and Workman, 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Neckers and Workman, 2012.

claim: Hsp90 inhibition promotes prostate cancer growth through Src kinase activation.
source: For example, Hsp90 inhibition promotes prostate cancer growth through Src kinase activation (Yano et al., 2008)
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Yano et al., 2008.

claim: Hsp90 inhibition favors breast cancer bone metastases formation.
source: and favors breast cancer bone metastases formation (Price et al., 2005).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Price et al., 2005.

claim: Over sixty percent of all cancers are glycolytic.
source: It is generally estimated that over sixty percent of all cancers are glycolytic.
evidence: This is a statement based on general knowledge in cancer biology.

claim: LATS1 signalization in the Hippo pathway is rendered ineffective in ovarian cancer xenograft tumors from mice treated with an Hsp90 inhibitor.
source: Consistent with this hypothesis and our data, LATS1 signalization in the Hippo pathway is rendered ineffective in ovarian cancer xenograft tumors from mice treated with an Hsp90 inhibitor (Huntoon et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Huntoon et al., 2010.

claim: MG was first viewed as a potential therapeutic agent in cancer.
source: MG is a potent cytotoxic compound and was first viewed as a potential therapeutic agent in cancer (Kang et al., 1996).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Kang et al., 1996.

claim: Hsp27 heat-shock protein is switched from a pro-apoptotic to an anti-apoptotic factor upon MG glycation.
source: Three independent groups have shown that Hsp27 heat-shock protein is switched from a pro-apoptotic to an anti-apoptotic factor upon MG glycation and facilitates cancer cell evasion from caspase-dependent cell apoptosis (van Heijst et al., 2006; Oya-Ito et al., 2011; Sakamoto et al., 2002).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to three studies.

claim: GLO1 is amplified in many types of human cancer with breast tumors (22%) and sarcomas (17%) showing the highest rates.
source: On one hand, the search for copy number changes on a large set of cancer cell lines revealed that GLO1 is amplified in many types of human cancer with breast tumors (22%) and sarcomas (17%) showing the highest rates (Santarius et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Santarius et al., 2010.

claim: A study aimed at functionally identifying tumor suppressor genes in liver cancer identified and validated GLO1 as a tumor suppressor gene which knockdown using shRNAs increased tumor growth in a mouse model.
source: On the other hand, a study aimed at functionally identifying tumor suppressor genes in liver cancer identified and validated GLO1 as a tumor suppressor gene which knockdown using shRNAs increased tumor growth in a mouse model (Zender et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Zender et al., 2008.

claim: Cell lines with GLO1 amplification or high Glo1 expression are reported to be much more sensitive to Glo1 inhibitors such as BBGC than those without.
source: Remarkably, cell lines with GLO1 amplification (Santarius et al., 2010) or high Glo1 expression (Sakamoto et al., 2001) are reported to be much more sensitive to Glo1 inhibitors such as BBGC than those without.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Santarius et al., 2010 and Sakamoto et al., 2001.

claim: GLO1 knockdown or inhibition using BBGC did not induce any significant cell apoptosis and hence conferred pro-growth and pro-metastatic advantages to breast cancer cells.
source: In our hands, GLO1 knockdown or inhibition using BBGC did not induce any significant cell apoptosis and hence conferred pro-growth and pro-metastatic advantages to breast cancer cells.
evidence: This claim is supported by the experimental data showing increased tumor growth and metastasis in GLO1-depleted cells (Figures 8 and 9).

claim: Many chemotherapeutic drugs used to treat cancer have been shown to exert their biologic activity through induction of oxidative stress.
source: Many chemotherapeutic drugs used to treat cancer have been shown to exert their biologic activity through induction of oxidative stress.
evidence: This is a statement based on established knowledge in cancer therapy.

claim: Compelling experimental and clinical evidence indicates that oxidative stress is diverted by cancer cells to promote their growth and resistance to apoptosis.
source: However, compelling experimental and clinical evidence indicates that this latter is diverted by cancer cells to promote their growth and resistance to apoptosis.
evidence: This is a statement based on existing literature about oxidative stress in cancer.

claim: MG dual effect has been shown recently for neurons where MG is favorable to neurons development and activity while high MG levels are toxic.
source: In a non-tumoral context, MG dual effect has been shown recently for neurons where MG is favorable to neurons development and activity while high MG levels are toxic (Radu et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Radu et al., 2012.

claim: Elevated blood concentrations of MG have been reported in type 2 diabetic patients.
source: Elevated blood concentrations of MG have been reported in type 2 diabetic patients (Nakayama et al., 2008)
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Nakayama et al., 2008.

claim: Plasma MG-derived hydroimidazolone was higher in type 1 diabetics as compared with non diabetics.
source: and plasma MG-derived hydroimidazolone was higher in type 1 diabetics as compared with non diabetics (Han et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Han et al., 2009.

claim: Recent studies indicated that cancer in diabetic patients presents with a higher incidence and a poorer prognosis than in non-diabetic persons.
source: Recent studies indicated that cancer in diabetic patients presents with a higher incidence and a poorer prognosis than in non-diabetic persons (Ryu et al., 2014; Xu et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Ryu et al., 2014 and Xu et al., 2014.

claim: Both MG scavengers metformin and carnosine have been shown to exert anti-tumoral effects.
source: Interestingly, both MG scavengers metformin and carnosine have been shown to exert anti-tumoral effects (Shen et al., 2014; Giovannucci et al., 2010)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Shen et al., 2014 and Giovannucci et al., 2010.

claim: Metformin proved efficient to reduce systemic MG levels in diabetic patients.
source: and metformin proved efficient to reduce systemic MG levels in diabetic patients (Beisswenger et al., 1999).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Beisswenger et al., 1999.

claim: Metformin, and its more potent analog phenformin, inhibited YAP activity through AMPK signaling.
source: DeRan and collaborators (DeRan et al., 2014) reported that metformin, and its more potent analog phenformin, inhibited YAP activity through AMPK signaling.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to DeRan et al., 2014.

claim: Metformin is a mitochondrial complex I inhibitor and a potent AMPK inducer.
source: Metformin is better known as a mitochondrial complex I inhibitor and a potent AMPK inducer, and it is somehow overlooked for its MG scavenging capacities.
evidence: This is a statement based on established knowledge about metformin's mechanisms of action.

claim: Alpha-oxoaldehydes are up to 20,000-fold more reactive than glucose in glycation processes.
source: Alpha-oxoaldehydes are up to 20,000-fold more reactive than glucose in glycation processes (Turk, 2010)
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Turk, 2010.

claim: It is expected that 1% to 5% of proteins in cells are modified by MG.
source: and it is expected that 1% to 5% of proteins in cells are modified by MG (Rabbani and Thornalley, 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Rabbani and Thornalley, 2014.

claim: MG leads to chemical modification of proteins, lipids and nucleotides that result in cellular dysfunction and mutagenicity.
source: MG leads to chemical modification of proteins, lipids and nucleotides that result in cellular dysfunction and mutagenicity.
evidence: This is a statement based on established biochemical knowledge about MG.

claim: MG interaction with amino groups of proteins notably leads to the formation of advanced glycation end products (AGEs) called hydroimidazolones (MG-H) and argpyrimidines.
source: MG interaction with amino groups of proteins notably leads to the formation of advanced glycation end products (AGEs) called hydroimidazolones (MG-H) and argpyrimidines (Thornalley, 1996).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Thornalley, 1996.

claim: All mammalian cells possess a detoxifying system constituted of glyoxalases 1 and 2 (Glo1 and Glo2, respectively), which catalyze the conversion of MG to D-lactate.
source: All mammalian cells possess a detoxifying system constituted of glyoxalases 1 and 2 (Glo1 and Glo2, respectively), which catalyze the conversion of MG to D-lactate (Thornalley, 2005).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Thornalley, 2005.

claim: MG-related AGEs have been found to be increased two- to fivefold and have been mainly identified in the context of diabetes.
source: At the molecular level, carbonyl stress is a common feature of the metabolic dysfunction associated with diabetes and cancer. MG-related AGEs have been found to be increased two- to fivefold and have been mainly identified in the context of diabetes.
evidence: This is a statement based on existing literature about MG-AGEs in diabetes.

claim: MG post-translational modification of vascular basement membrane type IV collagen has been associated with long-term diabetic complications.
source: For example, MG post-translational modification of vascular basement membrane type IV collagen (Dobler et al., 2006) and of voltage-gated sodium channel Nav1.8 (Bierhaus et al., 2012) have been associated with long-term diabetic complications.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Dobler et al., 2006.

claim: MG post-translational modification of voltage-gated sodium channel Nav1.8 has been associated with long-term diabetic complications.
source: For example, MG post-translational modification of vascular basement membrane type IV collagen (Dobler et al., 2006) and of voltage-gated sodium channel Nav1.8 (Bierhaus et al., 2012) have been associated with long-term diabetic complications.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Bierhaus et al., 2012.

claim: Only one study has reported MG-derived AGEs detection in malignant tumors.
source: To the best of our knowledge, only one study has reported MG-derived AGEs detection in malignant tumors (van Heijst et al., 2005).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to van Heijst et al., 2005.

claim: The formation of argpyrimidine on heat-shock protein 27 (Hsp27) prevented cancer cell apoptosis in lung and gastrointestinal cancers.
source: For example, the formation of argpyrimidine on heat-shock protein 27 (Hsp27) prevented cancer cell apoptosis in lung (van Heijst et al., 2006) and gastrointestinal (Oya-Ito et al., 2011) cancers.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to van Heijst et al., 2006 and Oya-Ito et al., 2011.

claim: Inhibition of MG modification on Hsp27 caused sensitization of cancer cells to antitumoral drugs.
source: Moreover, inhibition of MG modification on Hsp27 caused sensitization of cancer cells to antitumoral drugs (Sakamoto et al., 2002).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Sakamoto et al., 2002.

claim: MG has been shown to down regulate Hsp90 and Hsc70 expression levels in human retinal pigment epithelial cells.
source: MG has been shown to down regulate Hsp90 and Hsc70 expression levels in human retinal pigment epithelial cells (Bento et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Bento et al., 2010.

claim: Hsp90 stabilizes and activates more than 400 proteins, referred to as Hsp90 'clients', many of which are oncoproteins including transcription factors and kinases that are essential for cellular signal transduction pathways and adaptive responses to stress.
source: Hsp90 stabilizes and activates more than 400 proteins, referred to as Hsp90 'clients', many of which are oncoproteins including transcription factors and kinases that are essential for cellular signal transduction pathways and adaptive responses to stress (Trepel et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Trepel et al., 2010.

claim: LATS1 is a client protein of Hsp90.
source: One such client protein is the large tumor suppressor 1 (LATS1) (Huntoon et al., 2010)
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Huntoon et al., 2010.

claim: LATS1 is a key kinase that relays anti-proliferative signals in the Hippo pathway through Yes-associated protein (YAP) and transcriptional co-activator with PDZ-binding motif (TAZ) phosphorylation and inactivation.
source: a key kinase that relays anti-proliferative signals in the Hippo pathway through Yes-associated protein (YAP) and transcriptional co-activator with PDZ-binding motif (TAZ) phosphorylation and inactivation (Pan, 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Pan, 2010.

claim: The dysfunction of the Hippo signalization triggers tumorigenesis in human.
source: Consistent with its fundamental role in the control of organ growth and size in vertebrates, the dysfunction of the Hippo signalization triggers tumorigenesis in human (Harvey et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Harvey et al., 2013.

claim: YAP is a co-activator of TEAD family of transcription factors.
source: As a co-activator of TEAD family of transcription factors (Zhao et al., 2008)
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Zhao et al., 2008.

claim: YAP has been shown to enhance cancer progression through transcriptional activation of proliferation promoting genes such as c-myc and CTGF.
source: YAP has been notably shown to enhance cancer progression through transcriptional activation of proliferation promoting genes such as c-myc and CTGF (Moroishi et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Moroishi et al., 2015.

claim: 17-AAG, a potent Hsp90 inhibitor, disrupts LATS1 tumor suppressor activity in human cancer cells.
source: 17-AAG, a potent Hsp90 inhibitor, disrupts LATS1 tumor suppressor activity in human cancer cells (Huntoon et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Huntoon et al., 2010.

claim: Methylglyoxal (MG) is a highly reactive α-oxoaldehyde that is primarily formed in cells by the spontaneous degradation of triose phosphate intermediates of glycolysis, dihydroxyacetone phosphate and glyceraldehyde 3-phosphate.
source: Among those, methylglyoxal (MG) is a highly reactive α-oxoaldehyde that is primarily formed in cells by the spontaneous degradation of triose phosphate intermediates of glycolysis, dihydroxyacetone phosphate and glyceraldehyde 3-phosphate (Richard, 1993).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Richard, 1993.

claim: YAP/TAZ have been previously reported to promote EMT in human breast epithelial cells.
source: YAP/TAZ have been previously reported to promote EMT in human breast epithelial cells (Lei et al., 2008; Overholtzer et al., 2006).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Lei et al., 2008 and Overholtzer et al., 2006.

claim: Smad2/3 collaborate with TEAD and YAP to form an active transcriptional complex at CTGF promoter in breast cancer cells.
source: Smad2/3 collaborate with TEAD and YAP to form an active transcriptional complex at CTGF promoter in breast cancer cells (Hiemer et al., 2014; Fujii et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Hiemer et al., 2014 and Fujii et al., 2012.

claim: A previous study has shown that LATS1 kinase degradation occurs through polyubiquitination and the proteasome pathway in breast cancer cells.
source: A previous study has shown that LATS1 kinase degradation occurs through polyubiquitination and the proteasome pathway in breast cancer cells (He et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to He et al., 2016.
